searchText: Happy Saturday from Denver! I’m trying to understand the status of they Go implementation of discv5. I’m getting the impression there was a prototype implementation in go-ethereum that’s been removed. Specifically, this package seems to have changed course: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum@v1.9.25/p2p/discv5 Not sure if it was reorganized or simply dropped. Any pointers would be helpful. There are multiple different discovery packages in geth The one you're looking at is indeed a prototype/legacy kind of thing The package you're looking for is `discover`, it has both discv4 and discv5 in it. See https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/tree/master/p2p/discover <@!514629735339261993> if it helps, here's some example code (error handling is up to you): ```go import ( geth_log "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log" "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/p2p/discover" "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/p2p/enode" ) func example() { localNodeDB, err := enode.OpenDB(dbPath) // storage (empty path == in-memory db) localNode := enode.NewLocalNode(localNodeDB, priv) // your own ENR contents udpAddr := &net.UDPAddr{IP: net.ParseIP("0.0.0.0"), Port: 9000} conn, err := net.ListenUDP("udp", udpAddr) log := geth_log.New() log.SetHandler(geth_log.StdoutHandler) cfg := discover.Config{ PrivateKey: priv, NetRestrict: nil, Bootnodes: bootnodes, // list of enodes (parsed ENRs) Unhandled: nil, // Not used in dv5 Log: gethLogger, ValidSchemes: enode.ValidSchemes, } udpV5, err := discover.ListenV5(conn, localNode, cfg) } ``` Very helpful, thank you! Are you building something fun with discv5? Hopefully — I’m preparing to tackle state gossip within the stateless Ethereum roadmap that Piper has been roadmapping. My current status though is simply trying to catalog and vaguely understand some of the moving pieces ie: reading specs, locating implementations, figuring out how to operate them a bit That's going to be challenging. Yea, reading the discv5 specs would be good. Link: https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/master/discv5/discv5.md Thanks for that and agreed, lots to learn. I started with that doc this morning and ended up needing to learn what RLP was. Thankfully it’s all making sense, just no idea how deep the rabbit hole goes for me yet. I don’t think the rabbit hole ever ends but it’s one heck of a good journey. 🙂

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
<@!514629735339261993> if it helps, here's some example code (error handling is up to you):
```go
import (
    geth_log "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/p2p/discover"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/p2p/enode"
)
func example() {
    localNodeDB, err := enode.OpenDB(dbPath)  // storage (empty path == in-memory db)
    localNode := enode.NewLocalNode(localNodeDB, priv)  // your own ENR contents
    udpAddr := &net.UDPAddr{IP: net.ParseIP("0.0.0.0"), Port: 9000}
    conn, err := net.ListenUDP("udp", udpAddr)
    log := geth_log.New()
    log.SetHandler(geth_log.StdoutHandler)
    cfg := discover.Config{
        PrivateKey:   priv,
        NetRestrict:  nil,
        Bootnodes:    bootnodes,  // list of enodes (parsed ENRs)
        Unhandled:    nil, // Not used in dv5
        Log:          gethLogger,
        ValidSchemes: enode.ValidSchemes,
    }
    udpV5, err := discover.ListenV5(conn, localNode, cfg)
}
```
